'''Nándor Balázs''' ({{langx|hu|Balázs Nándor László}}; July 7, 1926{{spnd}}August 16, 2003)<ref name="zafra">{{cite web |url= http://ipht.cea.fr/Docspht/articles/t03/170/public/publi.pdf |title=Nándor Balázs |author1=de Zafra |author2=Bergeman |author3=Berry, Balian |author4=Voros |publisher=[[Institut de physique théorique - IPhT Saclay|Institut de physique théorique]] |location=Saclay, Paris |year=2008 |access-date=April 10, 2011}}</ref> was a [[Hungarian-American]] [[physicist]], and an external member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].

==Early life ==
Balázs attended Rácz private primary school where he was a classmate of [[John George Kemeny|Janos Kemeny]]. Balázs earned a master's degree at the [[University of Budapest]] (1948). Balázs left communist [[Hungary]] in 1949. He completed a [[PhD]] at the [[University of Amsterdam]] (1951).

==Career ==
Balázs spent 1951 and 1952 as assistant to [[Schroedinger]] at the [[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]],<ref>{{cite journal|author1=de Zafra, Robert |author2=Bergeman, Tom |author3=[[Michael Berry (physicist)|Berry, Michael]] |author4=[[Roger Balian|Balian, Roger]] |author5=Voros, André |title=Obituary: Nándor Balázs|journal=Physics Today|date=May 2004|volume=57|issue=5|pages=74|doi=10.1063/1.1768679|bibcode = 2004PhT....57e..74D |doi-access=free}}</ref> autumn 1952 through summer 1953 as assistant to [[Albert Einstein]] at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. He was associate professor of physics at the [[University of Alabama]] from 1953&ndash;56.  From 1956 to 1959, he was research associate at the [[Enrico Fermi Institute]] at the [[University of Chicago]], and became a research staff member at the [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory|Plasma Physics Laboratory]] at [[Princeton University]] from 1959 to 1961.<ref>Bognár, Desi K. (ed.), ''Hungarians in America: A Biographical Directory of Professionals of Hungarian Origin in the Americas''. Philadelphia: Afi Publication, 1971, 12.</ref> In 1961 he went to [[State University of New York at Stony Brook|Stony Brook University]].<ref name="sunysb">{{cite web |url=http://felix.physics.sunysb.edu/PAhist/nbalazs.html |title=Balázs, Nándor |last=Staff |work=State University of New York, Sunnybrook |year=2000 |access-date=April 10, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720014708/http://felix.physics.sunysb.edu/PAhist/nbalazs.html |archive-date=July 20, 2011 }}</ref> 

Balázs had close friendships and working collaborations with [[Erwin Schroedinger]], [[Paul Dirac]] (whose wife Margit Wigner was Hungarian), [[Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar]], [[Eugene Wigner]], and other prominent physicists.

Balázs maintained contacts in Hungary and occasionally brought Hungarian physicists to the US. In his collaborations with people in Budapest, such as Béla Lukács and József Zimányi, he dealt with relativistic heavy-ion collisions and thus provided a connection between Stony Brook (a home of RHIC theory) and Hungary.

==Works==

* Effect of a gravitational field, due to a rotating body, on the plane of polarization of an electromagnetic wave. Phys. Rev. 110, 236–239 (1958)

* EINSTEIN: Theory of Relativity. Gillispie (ed.) Dictionary of Scientific Biography, vol. IV, 319-332 (1971){{clarify|date=October 2024}}
